title: Improving young learners’ language practice and engagement through the BalaTalk digital platform
abstract: Introduction Young learners require repeated exposure, active participation, and sufficient time-on-task to develop vocabulary and oral language competence in Kazakh and Russian. Traditional primary classrooms, however, may not provide every pupil with frequent vocabulary repetition, immediate feedback, and equal opportunities for oral participation. This study examined the short-term effectiveness of the BalaTalk digital learning platform as a supplementary tool for language practice among third-grade pupils in Kazakhstan. Methods A quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test control group design was employed with 75 pupils from six intact classes across three schools. The intervention lasted one school week. Pupils in the experimental group used BalaTalk for 15-20 minutes per day during regular lessons, whereas pupils in the control group received traditional instruction without the platform. The assessed outcomes included vocabulary performance, oral speaking task performance evaluated using an analytical speaking rubric, and behavioral engagement operationalized as time-on-task. Teacher questionnaire responses and written parent feedback were collected as supplementary qualitative ev

title: Empirical studies on the development of music therapy training programs
abstract: This study examined experiential educational interventions for music therapy training in Japan, where opportunities for clinical practicum are limited. To address this educational challenge, simulated music therapy sessions were used as a controlled approximation of clinical interactions, although they cannot fully reproduce the complexity of real clinical practice. Two experiential approaches were investigated: physical imitation, in which participants reproduced a partner's movements, and eye closure, in which participants closed their eyes while listening to and interacting with the partner. The interventions were designed to engage different aspects of clinical listening, including attention to partners’ behaviors and sounds, emotional and intentional interpretation, and awareness of interpersonal interaction. Seventy-six undergraduate music students participated in a 2 × 2 factorial design examining physical imitation (present vs. absent) and eye closure (present vs. absent). Participants were assigned to therapist (Th) and client (Cl) roles and engaged in simulated music therapy sessions. title: Project-based learning technologies and the professional preparation of special education teachers in Kazakhstan
abstract: This study examines how project-based learning technologies contribute to the professional preparation of future special education teachers in Kazakhstan. A quantitative-supported qualitative research design was employed. The participants consisted of 76 undergraduate students and 11 professors from the History and Pedagogy/Special Pedagogy department at Uzbekali Zhanibekov South Kazakhstan Pedagogical University, selected through convenience sampling. Data were collected through a researcher-developed form including descriptive survey items and open-ended questions. Descriptive data were analyzed using frequencies and percentages, while qualitative responses were analyzed through content analysis. The findings showed that both students and professors conceptualized project-based learning as a practice-oriented approach that connects theoretical knowledge with real pedagogical situations. Participants emphasized that project-based learning contributed to diagnostic skills, corrective-developmental planning, individualized support, communication, collaboration, creativity, problem-solving, and professional confidence. title: Traditional and modern education systems in Ayurveda education: a critical integrative review
abstract: The evolution of Āyurveda education reflects a shift from an ancient, philosophically grounded educational model to a contemporary, institutionalized, competency-based one. Historically, Āyurveda was transmitted through the Gurukul system, a personalized, residential pedagogical model combining textual study with hands-on clinical training, emphasizing moral discipline ( Dharma ) and the Guru-Śiṣya Paramparā (teacher-disciple lineage). Learning was structured around the Trividha Jñānopāya (three-fold means of knowledge) and the cognitive sequence of Śravaṇa (listening), Manana (reflection), and Nididhyāsana (internalization). Colonial administrative frameworks and subsequent modernization transitioned Āyurveda education into a structured, time-bound, standardized university system. Today, under the governance of the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and guided by the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, Āyurveda education employs Competency-Based Medical Education (CBME), integrating digital technologies, Simulation-Based Learning (SBL), and objective assessment tools such as the Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE). title: Factors associated with Chinese vocational college students’ intention to use generative artificial intelligence for learning: an extended UTAUT mode
abstract: This study focuses on examining the factors influencing Chinese vocational college students’ behavioral intention to use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) for learning and further analyzing the relationships between these factors and changes in GenAI behavioral Intention. Based on the Unified Theory of behavioral Intention and Use of Technology (UTAUT), an extended model incorporating anxiety (ANX) was developed, and a two-stage analytical approach combining structural equation modeling (SEM) and ordered Probit (OProbit) regression was adopted. In the first stage, SEM was employed to examine the effects of various factors on behavioral intention within the extended UTAUT model. In the second stage, an OProbit model was applied, with changes in GenAI behavioral Intention specified as an ordinal outcome variable, to further examine the relationships between the relevant factors and changes in behavioral Intention while controlling for individual characteristics, including gender, grade level, and prior AI usage experience. title: Strategic leadership for agentic AI in education: a conceptual framework with reference to the United Arab Emirates
abstract: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) shifts educational leadership from whether to adopt a tool to which actions a configured system may take, under whose authority, and with what capacity for intervention and remedy. Through critical integrative synthesis of educational leadership, organisational decision-making, AI governance, and agentic-AI scholarship, this Conceptual Analysis develops educational agentic alignment: a relational judgement about whether delegated machine authority fits educational purposes, human decision rights, professional capabilities, safeguards, pedagogy, and public-value obligations. The focal unit is a dated and versioned educational delegation arrangement. The framework separates agentic capability, use-related exposure, and usable governance capacity; organises leadership decisions through seven domains across four levels; and proposes three mechanisms concerning safeguard shortfall, responsibility–capacity mismatch, and evidence-linked realignment. Each proposition specifies the analytical unit, variables, expected direction, measurable outcomes, time order, moderators, rivals, and evidence that would count against it. title: Artificial intelligence in university physics education: a systematic review of empirical studies
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into higher education, yet empirical evidence on its pedagogical use in university physics remains fragmented. This systematic review synthesized empirical research on the applications, reported learning and pedagogical outcomes, methodological quality, challenges, and educational implications of AI-supported university physics education. We used six search sources: SpringerLink, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and ERIC. The searches in the five original sources were updated through September 2026, and ERIC was added as an additional search source. Eligibility criteria were defined using the PICOS framework, study selection followed PRISMA 2020, and methodological quality was appraised using the 2018 Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Eleven empirical studies met the inclusion criteria and were synthesized narratively. Across the included studies, AI was used for tutoring and explanations, formative feedback and scaffolding, collaborative problem solving, simulation and modeling, instructional design, and developing AI literacy. title: Technology integration in basic school mathematics instruction: exploring teachers’ perceptions, readiness, and challenges
abstract: Despite growing recognition of technology as a catalyst for improving mathematics teaching and learning, its integration in basic school classrooms remains inconsistent, particularly in developing contexts where teachers often face pedagogical and contextual constraints. This study examined basic school teachers’ perceptions of technology incorporation in mathematics instruction, assessed their readiness for technology integration, and explored the challenges influencing its implementation. The study adopted an explanatory sequential mixed-method design involving 150 basic school mathematics teachers selected through stratified random sampling for the quantitative phase and five purposively selected teachers for the qualitative phase. Data were collected using an adapted structured questionnaire and a semi-structured interview guide. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics in SPSS (Version 27), while qualitative data were analysed thematically. The findings revealed that teachers generally held favourable perceptions of technology incorporation in mathematics instruction. title: Prompt-Mediated Curriculum Development: a human–AI co-design framework for AI-mediated curriculum development in higher education
abstract: The integration of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education is transforming curriculum development by enabling AI systems to contribute to the design of learning outcomes, assessments, instructional activities, and other curriculum artefacts. Despite growing interest in AI literacy, prompt engineering, and human–AI collaboration, limited attention has been given to how educators enact curriculum expertise within AI-mediated design environments. This conceptual paper introduces the Prompt-Mediated Curriculum Development (PMCD) framework, which conceptualises curriculum development as an iterative process of human–AI co-design mediated through prompt literacy. Drawing on curriculum theory, sociocultural perspectives on mediation, human–AI collaboration, and AI literacy scholarship, the framework positions prompt literacy as the central mechanism linking educator expertise, agentic AI systems, and curriculum artefacts. Prompt literacy is defined as the ability to formulate, refine, and evaluate prompts in ways that support pedagogically aligned and contextually relevant educational outcomes. title: Multilingual academic publishing in Kazakhstan: language shifts during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: This study aims to examine changes in the distribution of Kazakh-, Russian-, and English-language publications during and after the COVID-19 pandemic using the Eurasian Journal of Philology: Science and Education as a case study. The corpus comprises 535 articles published in Kazakh, Russian, and English between 2020 and 2025, including 278 articles from the pandemic period (2020–2022) and 257 from the post-pandemic period (2023–2025). The corpus was analysed using quantitative methods, keyword analysis, and scientometric techniques. Publication patterns were compared across the periods 2020–2022 and 2023–2025, with particular attention to the interplay between language choice, thematic focus, and the journal's disciplinary sections, including linguistics, literary studies, language teaching methodology, and translation studies. The findings reveal a statistically significant shift in the distribution of publication languages between the pandemic and post-pandemic periods, although the magnitude of the association was small. This shift was characterized by an increase in Kazakh-language publications from 38.1% to 47.1%, a decline in Russian-language publications from 30.2% to 21.0%

title: The future of virtual business education: students’ continuance intention in Colombian business schools
abstract: Colombian business schools are experiencing a transformation characterized by changing enrollment patterns, declining participation in some traditional face-to-face programs, and continued growth in virtual education. Drawing on a post-adoption perspective informed by the Expectation-Confirmation Model and the perceived-usefulness mechanism of the Technology Acceptance Model, this study examines the relationships of satisfaction, perceived usefulness, and perceived quality with students' continuance intention toward virtual classes. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 807 students enrolled in business-related programs at 12 private accredited universities in Bogotá, Colombia. Data were collected online between July 2024 and September 2025 using a non-probability sampling strategy combining convenience and snowball procedures. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. Satisfaction was the strongest predictor of continuance intention to use virtual classes ( β = 0.54, p < 0.001; f 2 = 0.29), followed by perceived usefulness ( β = 0.23, p < 0.001; f 2 = 0.08). title: Educommunication and artificial intelligence for learning, creating, and communicating: professional competency development in university prosumers
abstract: Introduction This study examines the pedagogical integration of educommunication and artificial intelligence (AI) and its association with self-reported professional competencies among university prosumers-students who simultaneously consume, produce, and share academic content through digital platforms. Methods A non-experimental, cross-sectional quantitative design with descriptive-correlational and structural purposes was employed. Data were collected using a psychometrically validated 26-item Likert-scale questionnaire (plus six open-response items) administered to a convenience sample of 547 university students enrolled at Universidad Politécnica Salesiana, Ecuador. The instrument assessed five dimensions: (1) AI-mediated learning processes, (2) educommunication and expression, (3) knowledge prosumption, (4) perceived professional competencies, and (5) ethics and critical AI use. Psychometric validation confirmed excellent reliability (Cronbach's α = 0.91; McDonald's ω = 0.93). title: Preparing pre-service teachers to understand and address cybersecurity challenges and promote digital citizenship in resource-constrained educational contexts: the role of 21st-century skills and technological knowledge
abstract: The availability and use of affordable mobile technologies offer significant opportunities for teachers to integrate technologies in their teaching, particularly in resource-constrained contexts. However, the availability and affordability of these digital tools do not guarantee their effective use. Their use also exposes teachers and learners to cybersecurity risks, and how well pre-service teachers (PSTs) are prepared to deal with those risks cannot be assumed. This study examines how PSTs are prepared to understand and address cybersecurity challenges and to promote digital citizenship in resource-constrained educational contexts. Preparation is examined along two dimensions: the 21st-century skills that PSTs demonstrate and the technological knowledge (TK) they acquire. This study was guided by the Cybersecurity Curriculum Framework, which integrates Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK), Digital Citizenship, and 21st-century skills. A qualitative approach was used. title: Empowering future educators: integrating artificial intelligence, sustainability, and ethics into teacher preparation programs
abstract: Teacher preparation programs have quickly adopted artificial intelligence tools, but the ethical, social, and environmental dimensions of that adoption receive comparatively little attention in how future educators are trained. This conceptual analysis addresses that gap by asking how AI competence, sustainability education, and ethical technology use can be integrated into teacher preparation as a single coherent framework rather than three parallel add-ons. Drawing on critical digital pedagogy, domain-specific cognition theory, and Mezirow's transformative learning theory, we synthesize policy documents and peer-reviewed literature on AI in education, sustainability education, and teacher preparation to develop the SAGE Model (Sustainability and AI for Global Educators). SAGE organizes teacher preparation around three interconnected pillars: Critical Integration, which addresses how AI systems reflect the assumptions and biases of their design; Applied Problem-Solving, which situates AI and sustainability literacy in authentic classroom and systems-level challenges; and Reflexive Praxis, which asks candidates to examine their own judgment and positionality when using AI tools. title: From eugenics to algorithms: structural racism in STEM and the imperative of liberatory reconstruction
abstract: This article argues that the exclusion of Black and other racially minoritized people from STEM is neither accidental nor remedied through incremental diversification. STEM's foundational structures includes its eugenics-entangled statistical canon, color-blind policy regimes, and systematic misdiagnosis of structural harm as individual deficit form an interlocking design of racial subordination. A primary argument for this article is that diversification without structural transformation is packaged and delivered as false prophets. Drawing on scholarship in critical race theory, Afrofuturism, critical quantitative and computational methodologies, and the mental and physical outcomes of these racialized STEM experiences, this article traces the historical construction of scientific racism from eugenics through contemporary algorithmic systems that perpetuate racial hierarchy under the sign of objectivity. The analysis proceeds in five sections. First, drawing on the historical record, this article contends that modern statistics are not neutral but constitutive of STEM's infrastructure. title: Developing interdisciplinary and meta-subject competencies in school geography: a systematic review of digital and mobile learning approaches
abstract: The integration of digital and mobile learning approaches into school geography has become an important direction of pedagogical innovation in recent years, however, how these approaches systematically develop interdisciplinary and meta-subject competencies remains insufficiently theorized and empirically developed. Although individual studies have demonstrated the pedagogical potential of geospatial technologies, mobile augmented reality, immersive virtual environments, and artificial intelligence-based platforms, no previous review has conducted a comprehensive, systematic analysis of this body of evidence, linking it to the cross-curricular and meta-subject competency frameworks that are central to the reform agenda for national and international curricula. The proposed study fills this gap through a systematic review conducted according to PRISMA 2020 requirements: Ninety-one peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2025 were included, selected from the Scopus database, and the level of agreement among the experts was confirmed with a κ = 0.79. title: Automated and AI-assisted assessment and perceived fairness in a polyethnic university: digitalization as a potential pathway to interethnic equity in Kazakhstan's higher education
abstract: The digital transformation of higher education in Kazakhstan unfolds against the backdrop of the 2022 constitutional reforms and the policy agenda of building a “Just Kazakhstan,” in which equal access to education for a multiethnic student population is a declared priority. This study examines how university students evaluate the fairness of automated and AI-assisted assessment, and whether such technologies are seen as reducing subjectivity, corruption risks, and ascriptive (ethnic and linguistic) bias. Respondents were not asked to compare formats within a single item, so the study reports perceptions of automated assessment rather than a measured contrast with examiner-based assessment. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 300 undergraduate and graduate students at a large public pedagogical university in Almaty (June 2026).
